name: Tamsulosin US pivotal studies
question: Does once-daily tamsulosin improve symptoms and peak urinary flow compared with placebo in men with symptomatic BPH?

design.population: 756 men with symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia were randomized in the primary US study.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 randomized trial

verdictNote: Both doses improved symptom score and peak flow; adverse events were higher at 0.8 mg.
takeaway: In the primary US phase 3 trial, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily or 0.4 mg for 1 week then 0.8 mg daily improved AUA symptom score and peak urinary flow versus placebo over 13 weeks; the higher-dose arm had more adverse events.

reports.label: Primary 13-week trial
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed give June 1998 only
reports.citation: Lepor H. "Phase III multicenter placebo-controlled study of tamsulosin in benign prostatic hyperplasia." *Urology.* 1998;51(6):892-900. doi:10.1016/s0090-4295(98)00126-5

results.measure: Change in total AUA symptom score at trial end
results.note: The abstract reports statistically significant improvement for both doses but gives no arm estimates or prespecified alpha.

results.measure: Change in Qmax at trial end
results.note: The abstract reports statistically significant improvement for both doses but gives no arm estimates or prespecified alpha.

delivery.label: Daily oral doses
delivery.value: Tamsulosin 0.4 mg or 0.8 mg once daily versus placebo.

reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed give June 1998 only

reports.followUp: 40-week extension after 13 weeks of randomized treatment

results.note: The abstract reports within-group improvement in all groups; it does not provide between-group estimates.
